task:
BUILD .fastops/worktree-compactor.js (under 120 lines). This tool ingests abandoned city worktrees into the city-ledger.

CONTEXT: There are 119 worktrees in .city-worktrees/. Each has a matching session JSON in .fastops/.sessions/<id>.json. The session JSON has: id, model, task, branch, status, history (turns with actions/results). Many worktrees have git commits with real work (code, patches, reports).

STEP 1: READ .fastops/city-ledger.js to understand the append API (CityLedger class, event requires: type, agent, action, optional data/tags/correlationId).
STEP 2: READ .fastops/.sessions/deepseek-mnka4gha-0dbc6f.json as a sample session file to understand the schema.
STEP 3: BUILD .fastops/worktree-compactor.js that:
  - Scans .city-worktrees/ for all directories
  - For each, reads the matching .fastops/.sessions/<id>.json (if exists)
  - Extracts: model, task, status, turn count, commit count (git log --oneline | wc -l), diff stat (git diff --stat HEAD vs parent branch)
  - Appends a ledger event per worktree: type='artifact_ingest', agent='worktree-compactor', action='ingest', data={sessionId, model, task, status, turns, commits, diffStat, branch}
  - Has a --dry-run flag that prints what would be ingested without writing
  - Has a --clean flag that deletes worktrees after ingestion (git worktree remove)
  - Handles missing session files gracefully (still ingest what git tells us)
STEP 4: EXEC 'node .fastops/worktree-compactor.js --dry-run' to validate it works on real data.
STEP 5: COMMIT and DONE.
